fine_lines.title: Type 1 vs Type 2 conditionals
fine_lines.explanation_ar: النوع الأول لحدث حقيقي محتمل: If you ignore it, it will fly away. النوع الثاني لحدث متخيَّل أو غير مرجّح: If all the bees died, there would be no food.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Type 1 is for a real, likely situation: If you ignore it, it will fly away. Type 2 is for an imagined or unlikely situation: If all the bees died, there would be no food.

fine_lines.title: will vs might vs may
fine_lines.explanation_ar: will = مؤكد تقريبًا. might و may = ممكن لكن غير مؤكد. Caroline صحّحت لآنا: you might get stung → you will get stung (مؤكد!).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Will = almost sure. Might / may = possible, not sure. Caroline corrects Anna: not 'you might get stung' but 'you will get stung'.

grammar.title: Conditionals: Type 1 and Type 2
grammar.explanation_ar: النوع الأول (حدث حقيقي ونتيجة محتملة جدًا): If + مضارع بسيط، will + فعل. مثال: If you talk to her, she'll help you. النوع الثاني (حدث متخيَّل أو غير مرجّح): If + ماضٍ بسيط، would + فعل. مثال: If all the bees died, there would be no food. يمكن أن نبدأ بالنتيجة: It will fly away if you ignore it (بدون فاصلة). ويمكن استخدام might / may بدل will عندما لا نكون متأكدين.
grammar.explanation_en: Type 1 (real event, likely result): If + present simple, will + verb. If you talk to her, she'll help you. Type 2 (imagined event): If + past simple, would + verb. If all the bees died, there would be no food. You can put the result first: It will fly away if you ignore it. Use might/may instead of will when you are not sure.
examples: If you ignore it, it will fly away.
If you swat it, it might sting you.
If all the bees died, there would be no food.
If you stay calm, the bees will be calm.
